title: Natural Law and Situation Ethics
welcome_lead: Set Aquinas's medieval synthesis against Joseph Fletcher's mid-twentieth century manifesto for love-based ethics.
meta_desc: A-Level Religious Studies adventure on Natural Law and Situation Ethics: primary precepts, double effect, Fletcher's six propositions.
final_note: You have contrasted rule-based and love-based Christian ethics on their foundational claims.

walkthroughs.body_html: In Summa Theologiae I-II QQ.90-97, Aquinas presents the four tiers of law and the primary precepts. Practical reason naturally pursues real goods rooted in human nature. Secondary precepts (no murder, no theft, etc.) are deduced from these. Acts are judged by object, intention and circumstance; intrinsically evil acts can never be justified.

The classic case: removing a cancerous womb that kills a foetus is permissible (the act is the removal of disease; the foetal death is unintended). Direct abortion is not (the act intends the death). Critics argue the distinction can be artificial; Philippa Foot's The Problem of Abortion and the Doctrine of Double Effect (1967) probed this with the trolley case.

Joseph Fletcher's Situation Ethics (1966) proposes six fundamental claims: only love is intrinsically good; the ruling norm is love; love and justice are the same; love wills the neighbour's good; only the end justifies the means; love decides situationally. Four working principles - pragmatism, relativism, positivism, personalism - frame his approach.

mcqs.q: Which is Aquinas's primary precept ordered to community?
options: Self-preservation
Reproduction
Education
Living in society

mcqs.q: The Doctrine of Double Effect requires that the bad effect be:
options: Greater than the good
Unintended
Forbidden by scripture
Inevitable

mcqs.q: What does natural law theory base morality on?
options: Situation ethics says rules should always be followed.
Natural law means whatever happens in nature is morally right.
Human nature and reason — there are objective purposes (telos) built into humans which reason can discover, generating universal moral precepts.
Natural law is the same thing as the laws of physics.

mcqs.q: What is the central principle of situation ethics?
options: Situation ethics says rules should always be followed.
Utilitarianism says you should always tell the truth.
You should do whatever feels right in the moment.
The only intrinsically good thing is agape love; rules can be broken if doing so produces the most loving outcome in the situation.

mcqs.q: What does utilitarianism say is right action?
options: The action that produces the greatest happiness for the greatest number — judged by consequences, not intentions or rules.
Utilitarianism says you should always tell the truth.
Natural law is the same thing as the laws of physics.
Whatever makes you personally happy is the right thing to do.

mcqs.q: How many fundamental propositions are in Fletcher's Situation Ethics?
Fletcher's working principle of personalism puts at the centre of ethics:
options: persons and their needs, rather than abstract rules
the commands of scripture
the maximisation of preference satisfaction
the cultivation of virtuous character

mcqs.q: A person who pursues wealth as their ultimate goal illustrates what Aquinas calls:
options: an apparent good — mistaking a limited good for true fulfilment
a real good that perfects human nature
the synderesis rule in action
an exterior act without an interior act

mcqs.q: Fletcher described conscience not as a faculty or voice but as:
options: a verb — the activity of making loving moral decisions in the situation
the super-ego internalising authority
an innate and infallible guide
the intellectual virtue of prudence

mcqs.q: Which pair are two of Fletcher's four working principles?
options: Pragmatism and positivism
Universalisability and autonomy
Synderesis and conscientia
Legalism and antinomianism

How many working principles does Fletcher list?
